data.content_ref: inline:{"claim": "Two conclusions are the same claim if they are always revised together as a minimal unit when the system encounters a contradiction and performs belief revision.", "mechanism": "The system employs an assumption-based truth maintenance system (ATMS). When a contradiction is detected, it identifies minimal sets of beliefs (nogoods) that must be revised. If two conclusions always appear together in the same minimal revision sets across all possible contradictions, they are considered the same claim. This is causal because identity depends on how the system repairs inconsistencies.", "scope": {"covers": ["conclusions within a nonmonotonic reasoning system with explicit justifications"], "excludes": ["conclusions in purely monotonic systems without revision"]}, "forbidden": [{"case": "Two conclusions are always revised together because they share a single justification, but they are intuitively distinct claims (e.g., 'Socrates is mortal' and 'All men are mortal' when the only justification for Socrates' mortality is the universal statement).", "eval": "program:check_revision_coupling"}], "prose_notes": "This mechanism identifies claims that are indistinguishable in the system's error-correction dynamics. It may over-merge if the revision granularity is coarse."}
